To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
alcohol devaluation reduces alcohol-related behaviour and attentional bias (AB), but does not reduce cue-elicited drinking.
alcohol devaluation reduced alcohol demand, AB, and choice in social drinkers and that AB fully mediated the effects of devaluation on cue-elicitation of alcohol seeking.
alcohol devaluation reduced alcohol choice, demand, craving and attentional bias.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of motivation in substance-related behaviour.
the mechanisms of substance motivation and behaviour.
understanding how alcohol motivation and behaviour is controlled.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
devaluing alcohol has a large effect on all indices of alcohol motivation, and that alcohol seeking is driven by a combination of goal-directed and cue-induced mechanisms.
alcohol behaviour in humans is largely sensitive to alcohol devaluation, i.c. governed by current drug motivational value.
alcohol-related behaviour is a heterogeneous phenomenon, and that different components of motivation may be more or less relevant depending on the behaviour being assessed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

alcohol behaviour is largely goal-directed, and that attentional biases may be important for both goal-directed and cue-induced alcohol seeking and consumption, and that the role of demand in alcohol seeking and consumption is more complex.

the motivational value of alcohol is a key determinant of alcohol behaviour in social drinkers and that attentional bias is a critical mediator of the effect of motivational value on alcohol-seeking and consumption.

the motivational value of a substance is important for the control of goal-directed substance-seeking behaviour but that the effects of this value on other forms of substance-seeking behaviour are less clear and may be mediated by other factors such as AB.
The main takeaway from our work is that
alcohol behaviour in social drinkers appears to be governed by a complex interaction of multiple motivational factors.
alcohol-related motivation and goal-directed behaviour are highly malleable and can be influenced by relatively minor manipulations, such as alcohol devaluation.
alcohol-related behaviour in social drinkers can be driven by different mechanisms.
